headline: Machine learning maps tissue and molecular profiles to cancer outcomes and subtypes
label: Tissue Profiling Outcome Models
summary: Tissue and molecular profiles are increasingly modeled against clinical endpoints, with benchmarks now testing how well these methods perform across cohorts…
synthesis: The dominant thread is machine learning that links tissue-level and molecular measurements to biological or clinical endpoints. Within this set, ovarian cancer work fuses patient-specific metabolic models derived from transcriptomics with 3D CT imaging to estimate survival, while quantum machine learning is applied to LUAD versus LUSC expression and methylation data to identify subtype biomarkers. Benchmarking is prominent: 22 unsupervised multi-omic subtyping methods are compared on TCGA-BRCA, and 10x and Parse single-cell platforms are compared on matched PBMCs. Foundation modeling appears in RNABag for pan-cancer classification, and cfDNA and ctDNA methods target liquid biopsy readouts. What is new is generative synthesis: Coherent Denoising creates missing omics and histopathology modalities from arbitrary input subsets.
